item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
+ Show Feedback
- Hide Feedback

It's my opinion that most of the entries on this page are of a quality that would not fly on the main list. For example, the use of the phrase [EXPLETIVE EXPUNGED] seems very out of place. This is particularly so given that this is not an interview or exploration log - it's appearing in written notes. These notes should be just as clinical as you would expect for any skip. The notes on SCP-1162 itself reflect this tone, to a certain degree, but most of the notes on the extended logs are variants on swearing, storytelling, literal quotes, and generally extraneous information.

I also take issue with the nature of some of these entries. At least a half dozen of them consist of people losing items from their person that were of value. The nature of this skip is well established - why would the Foundation continue to allow personnel to take in items that they were not prepared to lose? Once should be enough to prompt the Foundation to develop a certain protocol in testing to ensure that there are no repeats.

TL;DR: All in all, I believe that if this log in its entirety were posted today, it would not last very long on the site. While there are some good entries, the overwhelming majority are less than stellar, and really drag the tone of the testing log down. I'd love to see some serious pruning, but barring that, I'd at least like to see an improvement in the quality of entries being submitted in the future.

LEVEL 4 CLEARANCE REQUIRED
ACCESS GRANTED

Subject: Dr. V███
Note: Dr. V███ carried only a pen as a placeholder object. Test is to attempt to retrieve unaccounted-for container of SCP-008 believed to be in Russia. Proper sterilization and containment team standby in room.
Item Retrieved: Standard container of SCP-008, empty.
Item Lost: Dr. V███'s protective glove.
Notes: Dr. V███ was quickly quarantined and isolated for four (4) months. All bloodwork showed no infection of SCP-008, nor does Dr. V███ show any symptoms of infection. Container was devoid of any instance of SCP-008, suggesting that SCP-008 is still at previous location without any containment whatsoever. G2 sites report no missing containers. Current Russian and former USSR government(s) have been notified of containment breach.
